name: Monte Grande hollow
science_objective: Drill the Valle de la Luna bedrock in the Monte Grande hollow so CheMin and SAM can measure its mineralogy and volatiles, for comparison with a drill on the adjacent ridge.
why_it_matters: NASA says comparing the mineralogy, volatile content and organic chemistry of ridges and hollows should reveal how the boxworks formed. This is the hollow half of that pair.
position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4687, site 119, drive 1722 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row before the sol 4693 image; next row is sol 4709). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.
ez_theme: Hollow drill site: mineralogy and volatiles

evidence.text: Blog sols 4695-4701: Curiosity drilled its 44th hole at Valle de la Luna in the Monte Grande hollow; SAM evolved-gas analysis releases volatiles including H2O, CO2 and SO2.
Blog sols 4675-4681: the team chose Monte Grande as the next drill site, where SAM and CheMin will interrogate the boxworks.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).
